title: Harmonize PRD review journey across Eng / Design / Legal for acceptance gates
creator: Aisha Martinez
description: Objective: Create a lightweight, repeatable review and sign-off workflow for product requirement documents (PRDs) that reduces back-and-forth between Engineering, Design, and Legal and ensures deterministic acceptance criteria for shipping private and dedicated features. Scope: applies to all medium+ PRDs that change runtime behavior, billing flows, or customer-facing privacy surfaces (Private/VPC, Dedicated capacity, Console rollouts). Out of scope: small CLI fixes, trivial docs-only changes, or experimental spikes. Goals: 1) Make acceptance criteria explicit and testable. 2) Define owners and SLA for each review stage. 3) Produce a sign-off checklist that Legal can use without needing repeat briefings. 4) Reduce PRD review duration from ~8 days to <=3 business days for medium-scope PRDs.
acceptance_criteria: PRD includes a one-paragraph user story, list of affected routes/features, and a table of acceptance criteria mapped to test owners
Design has provided high-level mocks or annotated flows and a Figma link; outstanding UX issues are tracked in DES tickets
Engineering has provided an implementation approach, high-level perf/cost tradeoffs, and a list of required infra changes (ENG tickets created)
Legal confirms data categories impacted and provides required language for customer notices or contract addenda, or explicitly states no legal changes required
All three teams (PM/ENG/DES/LEGAL) have recorded explicit sign-off comments on the PRD document within the SLA window and assigned follow-up sub-issues where needed
Sign-off checklist completed and attached to PRD; PRD moves to Planned and linked to a Release/Iteration
tasks: Draft the 6-step PRD review playbook and publish to product wiki (owner: PM)
Create standard PRD template addendum that includes acceptance criteria table and reviewer roles (owner: PM)
Run a pilot with 'Dedicated autoscale' PRD and capture timings and blockers (owner: PM + Eng lead)
Iterate on slate of example sign-off language for Legal to reuse (owner: Legal)
Add a required metadata block on PRD front page with reviewer SLA fields and auto-notifications (owner: Design/Eng tooling)
Train 1 cross-functional squad on the new flow and collect feedback (owner: PM)
Instrument a small dashboard measuring average review time and number of review cycles per PRD (owner: Analytics)
Create webhook template to notify reviewers when PRD moves states (owner: Eng)
Publish a one-page cheat sheet for engineers and designers on 'What Legal needs' (owner: Legal)
Finalize the sign-off checklist and create a PRD-to-release link policy (owner: PM)
notes: Context: multiple recent PRD delays observed for private deployment features; common failure modes: unclear acceptance criteria, late legal involvement, and shifting UX scope.
Trade-offs: tighter SLAs increase upfront PM effort and may lead to more initial rework; should reduce downstream waste and accelerate delivery.
Fallbacks: if Legal cannot complete a formal review within SLA, accept an explicit 'Legal triage' note with required follow-ups and gating conditions for release.
